motion.implementation: Express offsets as --sx/--sy and derive the hover translate from them: box-shadow:var(--sx) var(--sy) 0 0; :hover{transform:translate(var(--sx),var(--sy));box-shadow:0 0 0 0}. A size variant changes only --sx/--sy. Re-declaring box-shadow in a variant wins on source order and leaves the shadow behind on hover.

focus.reason: resting border is already black, so a black ring is a 0-pixel change and fails WCAG 2.4.13. An accent ring also fails: 2.37:1 over the #dfe5f2 page tint, the pixels the ring occupies

spacing.reason: the 4px hover shift plus the 4px shadow needs clearance or it reads as a jump / clips at the edge

copyBudget.note: tighter than the engine default of 8 words / 420 chars because the display type is large

darkMode.rule: the border and shadow invert to white; the accent does NOT change. A black border on a dark ground erases every affordance at once.
darkMode.accentTextRule: Text on an accent-filled surface hard-codes color:#000 in BOTH themes. The accent does not invert; inheriting --border yields white-on-blue at 3.23:1, below the 4.5 floor.

notes.tokens: Four numbers do all the work — 2px border, 4px shadow offset, 0 blur, 5px radius. Every value was read out of the live theme on neobrutalism.dev via getComputedStyle, not sampled from a screenshot.
notes.nav: Full-width bar, no shadow at rest — a 4/4 shadow implies a floating card, and a bar spanning the viewport is not floating. It earns a shadow only once it sticks, and then only on y: a full-bleed bar has no right edge to cast from. That is the one sanctioned exception to global shadow direction.
notes.hero: Engine §5 caps a headline at 8 words. This pack caps it at 6, because the display type is large enough that 8 wraps to four lines. No shadow on the hero container — shadows belong to things you can act on.
notes.button: Focus is the state this pack nearly fails. The resting border is already black, so a black ring is a 0-pixel change and fails WCAG 2.4.13. An accent ring fails too, and not for the obvious reason: accent on white is 3.23:1 and passes, but the ring is drawn in pixels that were page tint, where it measures only 2.37:1. Hence a white gap then a black ring.
notes.form: Inputs carry no resting shadow — an input is a well, not a raised object. Only the submit button is raised. Without that distinction a form looks like a pile of identical bricks. The error border stays black: a red border alone is colour-only signalling (WCAG 1.4.1).
notes.card: The pack's default object. Nested radius is calc(5px - 2px) = 3px. Cards in a grid need ≥8px gap — the 4px hover shift plus the 4px shadow needs that clearance or the hover reads as a collision.
notes.table: Where this pack is strongest: hard rules are already its native vocabulary. Radius on the outer container only; cells are square, clipped by overflow:hidden. No zebra striping — the 2px rules already separate rows, and a tint would be a third value against the two-hue budget.
notes.overlay: Scrim is 80% black with no blur. Depth comes from the scrim, not from a bigger shadow — the temptation is to scale the shadow to signal elevation; resist it. The close button is 32×32 because icon-only controls need explicit sizing; padding alone will not clear WCAG 2.5.8.
notes.empty: The missing shadow is the message — there is no object here yet. Dashed is the one place the solid-border rule bends, and it bends deliberately: dashed reads as a slot. Loading uses flat blocks and no shimmer, because a shimmer is a gradient.
notes.dark: Not a background swap. A black border on a dark ground disappears — and in this pack the border is the entire affordance system. Border and shadow invert to white; the accent does not. And because the accent does not invert, text on the accent must not either — hard-code color:#000 or dark mode gives you white-on-blue at 3.23:1.
notes.narrow: The shadow extends 4px right and down, so at 0 page padding it clips. 16px page padding is a floor, not a preference. On touch there is no hover — but there is :active, and it moves 5px.
notes.copy: 380 chars per viewport, under the engine's 420, because the display type is larger.
